item.title: Many Iranians are heading to Turkey to escape the ongoing war's heavy toll
item.description: Iranians visiting the city of Van, Turkey, near the Iranian border say how expensive and difficult life back home is.

item.title: Democrats grapple with Trump's push to limit transparency within the executive branch
item.description: President Trump is pushing the boundaries of executive power to limit transparency within the executive branch. Congressional Democrats are grappling with how to respond.

item.title: Judge knocks down a National Firearms Act provision, handing win to gun rights groups
item.description: A federal judge's decision out of Texas has major implications for the National Firearms Act, lifting regulations on certain guns and suppressors in more than a dozen states.

item.title: Why some companies are paying more than $1 million to get through the Panama Canal
item.description: With the Strait of Hormuz effectively closed, pressure on the Panama Canal has increased. And combined with lower water levels, transit prices through the canal are soaring.

item.title: In 'The Wrong Girls,' Kristen Stewart and Alia Shawkat play messy stoner BFFs
item.description: NPR's Ailsa Chang talks with Dylan Meyer about her directorial debut, The Wrong Girls and the value of seeing women being silly and making dubious decisions onscreen.

item.title: Should the U.S. have a mandatory retirement age?
item.description: Older workers are delaying retirement more and more. But it's causing younger workers to wonder if they're missing out on job advancement because senior roles aren't opening up. Is this true?

item.title: Remembering Zhu Rongji, the architect of China's modern economy
item.description: The staggering pace of China's economic growth these past four decades has been historic. The chief architect of the financial reforms that made way for that growth died on Wednesday at age 97.

item.title: A week of rain displaces thousands in Midwest floods
item.description: Evacuations orders continue to be issued in Ohio following days of rain that has washed out roads and caused widespread flooding across Indiana and Illinois, too.

item.title: At Big Bend National Park, bulldozers begin clearing land for border barrier work
item.description: In the Big Bend area of West Texas, contractors are beginning to set the stage to build the Trump administration's planned border wall and barriers, despite bipartisan opposition.
